main_text.head: PERICOPA PRIMA
Querelam vatis de sui temporis corruptione completens.
EXPOSITIO LITERALIS.
Verf. 1. Prolatio verbi, quod vidit Habaccuc propheta.
main_text.p: §. 1.VOX הַמַּשָּׂא à themato מַשָּׂא non eodem modo vertitur ab interpretibus. Multi per vocem onus reddunt, atque onerosām prophetiam exponunt, cujus argumentum est praedicere graviora Dei judicia: in quam sententiam Hieronymus concedens, dixit; quod vox MASSA nunquam praeferatur in titulo, nisi cum grave & ponderis laborisque plenum est, quod videtur. Verum id semper obtinere non videbitur conferenti vaticinia, quae populo Dei spem faciunt maximarum Dei promissionum, omniaque fausta & laeta ad ejusdem solatium spondent: ut fieri videmus, Zach. 12: 1. Conf. Thren. 2: 14. Notandum verbum נָשָׂא (cui haec vox suam debet originem) inter varias potestates etiam praeconis designare opus, atque elationem vocis praeconian-tis significare, quod videre licet Num. 23: 17. 38: 3. Job. 27: 1. Jes. 14: 4. Hinc Cl. Coccejus prolatio-nem reddit, atque pro eloquio publico, seu concione prophetica poni agnoscit, arcanum Dei consilium inter homines exponente, atque ita decretum Dei revelatum

page.notes: Drop-cap initial V of "VOX" is a woodcut ornament; the letter is read as V. The Hebrew words in the first sentence (the first is printed as a lone word, the second after "à themato") are doubtful: [?] was not placed because the Hebrew is small and blurred, so the letters are a best reading and should be checked. The Hebrew at "verbum" is also a best reading. A small asterisk follows "EXPOSITIO LITERALIS." and is not transcribed as text. The Greek/Hebrew forms are copied as seen, not from memory. The printed line "pro-" at the foot is the catchword and is not repeated in the text. Printed hyphens kept at "praeconian-tis" and "prolatio-nem".
